semantic_correction.stem: After an inpatient dies by suicide, several staff members and clients who knew the person are distressed. Which organizational response best reflects suicide postvention and patient-safety principles?

options.A: Offer support to distressed people and delay the organizational safety review until grief reactions subside so investigation does not interfere with healing.
options.B: Begin a systems review immediately and postpone staff and client support until contributing factors and individual accountability have been established.
options.C: Provide immediate and ongoing support to affected people while a separate systems review examines contributing factors and actions to reduce recurrence.
options.D: Complete required records and notify leadership, but leave grief support to individuals and defer a broader safety review unless an outside authority requests it.

semantic_correction.rationale: VA Uniting for Suicide Postvention describes suicide postvention as providing immediate and ongoing support to people affected by a suicide loss and emphasizes support for providers and workplaces after a suicide. Separately, Joint Commission patient-safety policy emphasizes learning from serious safety events through investigation and analysis, including examination of root causes and contributing factors and implementation of improvements intended to reduce recurrence. These functions are complementary rather than sequential substitutes for one another. Therefore C is the best response: affected people receive timely support while the organization also conducts a separate systems-focused safety review. A unnecessarily delays safety learning, B postpones needed postvention support and shifts emphasis toward individual accountability, and D omits proactive postvention and systems learning.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: After a suicide death, provide organized immediate and ongoing support to affected clients and staff while participating in a separate systems-focused patient-safety review of contributing factors and corrective actions to reduce future risk.
semantic_correction.source_organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Rocky Mountain MIRECC for Suicide Prevention; Joint Commission

semantic_correction.source_version_date: VA USPV About page last updated December 4, 2025 and rechecked August 20, 2026; Joint Commission Sentinel Event Policy effective January 1, 2026 and current FAQs rechecked August 20, 2026, including announced January 1, 2027 alignment transition
semantic_correction.source_locator: VA USPV About: suicide postvention builds on prevention by providing immediate and ongoing support to those impacted by suicide loss and is critical to foster healing. Joint Commission Sentinel Event Policy: investigation and analysis of patient safety events and evaluation of corrective actions are essential to reduce risk and prevent harm; policy encourages root cause/comprehensive systematic analysis and plan of action. Current Sentinel Event FAQs: accredited organizations are expected to identify sentinel events, examine root causes and contributing factors, and make improvements to mitigate recurrence; that expectation remains during the 2027 alignment transition.
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Suicide postvention includes immediate and ongoing support for people affected by a suicide loss, while healthcare patient-safety frameworks separately use systems-focused investigation of root causes/contributing factors and corrective actions to reduce recurrence risk.

semantic_correction.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — suicide postvention, grief support, and systems-based safety review
semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup retained the postvention plus systems-review construct, rebuilt A/B/C/D so the key is not uniquely longest, and separated psychosocial support from systems-focused event analysis rather than treating either as a substitute for the other.

scope_exclusions.sentinel_event_reporting: The item does not claim that external reporting to Joint Commission is mandatory; Joint Commission reporting remains voluntary.
scope_exclusions.event_classification_details: The item does not test the technical inclusion criteria or timing rules used to classify a particular event under current or future Sentinel Event definitions.
scope_exclusions.blame: The systems review is framed around contributing factors and corrective actions; the item does not assert that individual accountability is never relevant when facts warrant it.
scope_exclusions.postvention_duration: No fixed duration of postvention support is prescribed; support is described as immediate and ongoing according to need.
scope_exclusions.specific_referral: No named grief program, hotline, or mandatory referral pathway is tested.
scope_exclusions.blueprint_precision: NCSBN explicitly supports grief/loss care and performance/quality improvement; it does not explicitly name suicide postvention or root-cause analysis in the cited top-level activity statements.

near_duplicate_check.note: Targeted GitHub search for ‘suicide postvention immediate ongoing support staff clients system factors root cause recurrence sentinel event’ returned no indexed repository match. No broad bank scan was performed.

option_audit.A: Plausible because emotional support is appropriate and poorly timed investigation can feel burdensome, but serious safety learning should not be deferred until grief has resolved.
option_audit.B: Plausible because systems analysis is necessary after serious safety events, but postvention support should not be withheld while that analysis occurs and the response should not begin from a blame-first frame.
option_audit.C: Correct. It combines timely postvention support with a separate systems-focused review of contributing factors and recurrence-reduction actions.
option_audit.D: Plausible because documentation and leadership notification are expected organizational activities, but the response is incomplete if it leaves grief support entirely to individuals and conditions safety review on an external request.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. C alone preserves both evidence-supported postvention and systems learning concurrently. A delays review, B delays support and centers individual accountability, and D omits proactive support and internal safety learning.

cueing_check.note: The key is tied with B for shortest and is not uniquely verbose; all four are organizational-response statements with comparable detail.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: The item integrates explicit Psychosocial Integrity grief/loss and coping-support activities with explicit Management of Care participation in performance/quality improvement.
